newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures falter, May clings at $1,500.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures falter, May clings at $1,500.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures recouped some lost ground by the close on industry price-fixing after an earlier fund led sell-off, traders said.
An avalanche of trade hedge sales helped drive prices sharply lower early in the session as the market took a cue from New York's steep decline the day before.
London was called $100-$115 off at the open. But it managed to gap just $75 lower basis May.
Prices then sea-sawed before standing $49 weaker on the day at $1,506 at the close.
Investment funds, holding sizeable long positions built up during the recent market rally, were also seen rolling forward some of their nearby holdings.
Major fund sell-stops were seen at below $1,500 on May. But traders said fresh roaster buying on the dips helped the contract to close above $1,500.
Overall volume was an impressive 9,147 lots.
New York arabica futures were weaker this morning on speculative selling ahead of the March first notice day on Thursday.
Traders took note of a crop forecast released by Brazil's exporter group Abecafe which pegged the coming 1997/98 harvest at 23.2 million 60-kg bags.

While the forecast was higher than earlier Brazilian officials' suggestion of between 18 and 20 million, traders said the 23.2 million was more or less in line with market expectation of 23-24 million bags.
"I don't think many people took below 20 million very seriously but I might be wrong," said one. "I think 23 million is a reasonably interesting number."

The Brazilian forecast, based on a survey of 23 of 45 companies which belong to Brazilian Coffee Exporters' Association (Abecafe), was made public by the secretary-general of the association, Jose Sette, in Sau Paulo.
No figure was given for the 1996/97 crop. Of the total, some 18.7 million bags are forecast to be of arabica coffee and 4.5 million bags of robusta coffee.
